title: Fuel Is One of Your Biggest Costs, So Why Doesn’t Anyone Know Where It’s Going Until Month-End?
summary: Learn how continuous fuel monitoring uncovers hidden fuel losses, improves accountability, and reduces fleet operating costs.
body_text: TL;DR: One-Minute Brief A fuel bill comes in higher than expected, and the only way to explain it is to reconcile fuel-card receipts against odometer readings a month after the fact, by which point theft, siphoning, or a leak has already had weeks to continue unnoticed. This blog covers why fuel is simultaneously one of the biggest and least visible costs in fleet operations, and how tracking every tank and every machine continuously, flagging real fuel-level changes with a confidence score, and giving investigators a full event replay turns a monthly guessing game into a same-day investigation. A Fuel Bill Lands Over Budget, and Nobody Can Explain Why The fuel bill comes in higher than expected. The finance team asks operations to explain it. Operations pulls fuel-card statements and cross-references them against odometer readings and hour meters, machine by machine, and two days later still cannot say with confidence whether the gap is theft, a leak, unusually heavy idling, or simply a data entry error somewhere in the chain. By the time the numbers are reconciled, whatever was actually happening, siphoning at a yard, a slow leak in a tank, an operator running the engine for hours without doing any productive work, has had a full reconciliation cycle to keep happening completely undetected. For most fleets, fuel is one of the largest controllable line items in the entire operating budget, and also one of the least visible in real time. That combination is what makes it so expensive. It is not that fleets do not care about fuel cost. It is that the only tool most of them have to monitor it is a monthly comparison between what was purchased and what the vehicle appears to have used, and a comparison run once a month can only ever catch a problem once a month too. What Actually Counts as Abnormal Fuel Behavior? Abnormal fuel behavior is any sudden, unexplained change in a machine’s or a tank’s fuel level that does not match what the equipment was actually doing. A tank level that drops faster than any refuel or normal burn rate can explain is one example. A vehicle whose fuel consumption climbs while its actual working activity stays flat is another. The distinction that matters most is separating fuel spent on real work from fuel spent on nothing: an engine left running while a machine sits idle still burns fuel and shows up on the bill, even though it delivered zero output, and unless that idling fuel is tracked separately from productive fuel use, it hides inside a single combined total where nobody can see it. Why Does Investigating a Fuel Anomaly Take So Long? Most fleets do not struggle to eventually notice that fuel spend looks wrong. They struggle to investigate it fast enough for the answer to still be useful. Fuel-card data lives in one system, vehicle location and activity data lives in another, and any additional context, who was assigned to the vehicle, what site it was working, often lives in a supervisor’s notes or a phone thread. Matching a spike in the fuel-card statement to a specific machine, shift, and cause means manually cross-referencing sources that were never built to talk to each other. It also does not help that a fuel-level sensor is not perfectly precise. Ordinary sloshing, temperature changes, and reading noise can all make a fuel gauge look like it moved even when nothing actually happened. Without a way to separate a genuine drop or refill from that kind of noise, teams either chase false alarms or, more commonly, stop trusting the alerts altogether and fall back on the slower monthly reconciliation they were trying to avoid in the first place. By the time anyone sorts out what is signal and what is noise, the shift has ended, the operator has changed, and the machine has moved to another site. The window to gather real evidence closes fast. How Do Manual Fuel Investigations Typically Play Out? A typical manual fuel investigation looks something like this: Export fuel-card or bulk tank refill records for the past thirty days. Pull hour meter and odometer readings per asset from spreadsheets or separate OEM apps. Call site supervisors or operators to confirm shift assignments and any route or schedule changes. Manually calculate expected consumption per hour and compare it against actual fuel drawn. Escalate to finance only once the numbers clearly fail to add up, weeks after the underlying event happened. Every one of those steps depends on someone logging something correctly the first time. One missed hour meter reading, or one supervisor who is out sick that week, and the investigation stalls for another cycle entirely. What Does Fast, Evidence-Backed Fuel Detection Actually Look Like? Fast detection starts with tracking fuel level continuously, for every machine and every stationary tank, rather than waiting for a reconciliation process to catch a discrepancy weeks later. When a fuel level changes abruptly, the change is classified immediately as either a fuel drop, a candidate for theft, siphoning, or a leak, or a refill. Every one of those detected events carries a confidence score reflecting how certain the system is that this is a genuine change rather than sensor noise, and the number of minor fluctuations filtered out as noise is disclosed rather than hidden, so a team reviewing the data can trust what they are being shown instead of chasing false alarms. Once an event is flagged, it can be opened into a full, synchronized replay: fuel level, vehicle speed, engine RPM, fuel consumption data, GPS location, and ignition state, all moving together on one timeline with adjustable padding before and after the event. That gives an investigator the ability to see exactly what the vehicle was doing at the precise moment fuel disappeared or was added, turning a suspicious number on a spreadsheet into a documented, evidence-backed sequence rather than a guess. Every reviewed event can also be marked as accurate, inaccurate, or needing further attention, which feeds a loop that improves detection quality over time instead of treating every fleet the same way from day one. Alongside theft and leak detection, the same continuous tracking separates working fuel from idling fuel for every machine and reports efficiency in distance per liter, surfacing what is often the single largest controllable source of waste in a fleet: engines left running without the vehicle actually doing anything. That same tracking extends beyond vehicles to stationary bulk fuel tanks, using the same current-level, refill, and consumption view, so a yard tank is monitored with the same rigor as a truck on the road. Manual Fuel Reconciliation vs. Continuous Fuel Monitoring Factor Manual Reconciliation Continuous Fuel Monitoring Data sources Fuel cards, spreadsheets, phone calls Unified per-asset fuel, activity, and location data Detection speed Days to weeks, usually at month-end Minutes, as the event happens Granularity Fleet-wide or vehicle-level averages Per-asset, per-event Confidence in an alert Based on manual judgment A disclosed confidence score plus filtered-out noise count Investigation evidence Reconstructed after the fact, if records still exist Synchronized replay of fuel, speed, RPM, location, and ignition Common Mistakes That Slow Down Fuel Investigations Most delays come from a handful of repeatable habits, not one dramatic failure: Tracking fuel spend at the fleet level instead of per asset. Waiting for month-end reconciliation instead of continuous alerts. Treating every fuel-level fluctuation as equally suspicious, which trains teams to ignore alerts altogether. Keeping fuel-card data, activity data, and site notes in separate systems that are never cross-referenced in real time. Lumping idling fuel in with productive fuel use, which hides one of the largest sources of waste inside a single combined number. Why Fuel Visibility Matters More Right Now Fuel remains one of the largest controllable costs on a fleet’s balance sheet, and margin pressure keeps increasing as competition for large contracts tightens. At the same time, sustainability commitments across the region mean fuel data increasingly doubles as emissions data, so a slow fuel investigation is not just a cost problem anymore. It is a reporting gap too, one that shows up in exactly the compliance conversations clients and regulators are asking fleets to be ready for. How TENDERD Helps Cut Fuel Investigation Time TENDERD’s Fuel Intelligence platform is built to close the gap between a fuel anomaly happening and someone finding out. Every machine and stationary tank is tracked continuously, with fuel drops and refills flagged automatically and assigned a confidence score, and every event can be opened into a full replay correlating fuel level, speed, RPM, location, and ignition state on one timeline. Based on analysis of anonymized data from TENDERD customers, fleets typically see roughly a 25 percent reduction in emissions and fuel wastage from idling within a year of adoption, simply from being able to see and act on waste that was previously invisible. At McDermott’s Jebel Ali yard, where the team had no live visibility into fuel burn or misuse across more than 1,000 yard and barge assets, this approach cut fuel use by 8 percent while lifting productivity. The Bottom Line Fuel does not need to remain a monthly mystery. The fleets that control fuel cost best are the ones that can see a drop or a refill the moment it happens, know how confident they should be that it is real, and have the evidence to act on it immediately, rather than waiting for a reconciliation cycle to confirm what already happened weeks ago. Want to see how much fuel loss is currently hiding inside your monthly reconciliation? Talk to the TENDERD team about a Fuel Intelligence walkthrough: Book a Demo Frequently Asked Questions Why is fuel one of the hardest costs for fleets to control? Fuel spend is usually only reconciled once a month against fuel-card receipts and odometer readings, so any theft, siphoning, or leak has weeks to continue before anyone notices the discrepancy, and by then the cause is difficult to trace. How can fleets tell a real fuel loss apart from a sensor glitch? Continuous fuel monitoring can assign a confidence score to every detected drop or refill, distinguishing genuine fuel-level changes from sensor noise, and disclose how many minor fluctuations were filtered out so nothing is hidden from the person reviewing the data. What is idling fuel, and why does it matter? Idling fuel is fuel consumed while a machine's engine is running but the machine is not actively working. It is often the single largest controllable source of fuel waste in a fleet, and it stays invisible unless it is tracked separately from fuel used during actual work. How does an operator investigate a suspected fuel theft event? A flagged fuel event can be opened into a synchronized replay showing fuel level, speed, engine RPM, GPS location, and ignition state together on one timeline, letting an investigator see exactly what the vehicle was doing at the moment the fuel level changed. Does fuel monitoring cover stationary storage tanks as well as vehicles? Yes. Bulk, stationary fuel tanks are tracked with the same current-level, refill, and consumption view used for vehicles, so yard and depot fuel storage gets the same visibility as fuel used in the field.

title: Meeting the horizontal electroless copper plating challenge
summary: How Qnity addresses reliability demands and increased complexity of HDI and IC package substrates.
body_text: Electronic devices have become an indispensable part of people’s daily life in every corner of the globe. Performance of such devices is evolving at a tremendous rate, driven by both semiconductor technology and software advances. In recent years, along with the reduction in size and increased performance of electronic devices, the packaging density of electronic circuits has become higher and subsequently required to be defect-free after electroless plating. The most commonly used method to catalyze or activate laminated non-conductive dielectric substrate regions, prior to electroless plating, is to treat the board with an aqueous palladium-tin colloid in an acidic medium. As a result of greater demands on reliability and the increased complexity of these high-density-interconnect (HDI) and integrated circuit (IC) package substrate boards, new innovations are necessary to meet these metallization requirements. Novel catalysts expand our portfolio beyond the current Pd/Sn colloidal catalyst technologies, which have been used commercially as activators for electroless metal deposition for decades, and enable our customers to meet the ever increasing performance demands. In this post, we introduce Circuposit™ 6530 Catalyst developed specifically for horizontal electroless Cu plating. Catalytic systems based on ionic solutions have several important advantages over the colloidal catalysts currently employed. The ionic catalyst complexes have intrinsically superior stability to oxidizing environments, such as the high agitation typically found in horizontal conveyorized equipment, due to the absence of extraneous metal ions, particularly Sn2+. Additionally, the ionic catalyst complexes enable penetration and surface activation of even the deepest substrate recesses while maintaining wide operating parameters with ease of process control. Finally, these catalysts provide the reduced residual conductivity necessary for fine line technology typically found in these complex designs. For these high density interconnects, horizontal processing is the preferred technology given that a conveyorized system can more readily handle thin core processing. Additionally, the improved solution flow can easily meet the uniformity requirements of these complex microstructures on both sides of the panels through consistent catalyst application and chemical treatment. High-end structures also require multiple metallization cycles, wherein productivity is an issue, giving horizontal processing the advantage. In response to customer needs for a drop-in solution for HDI and IC package substrate boards plated in horizontal conveyorized equipment, Dow Electronic Solutions developed the Circuposit™ 6530 Catalyst, an ionic palladium catalyst designed specifically for use in this application. The ionic palladium catalyst demonstrates stable bath life and reliable performance over a wide process window. It provides high reliability performance by ensuring uniform coverage throughout features while maintaining high Cu-Cu joint reliability to withstand the physical, thermal, and chemical stresses of additional processing as well as throughout the final device life. Want to learn more? Read the paper titled “ Circuposit™ 6530 Catalyst Process for Electroless Copper Metallization ,” which details the reliability performance and horizontal electroless Cu plating processes using this formulation, and has been presented on Oct. 22 at the 2015 IMPACT Forum.

title: Deel vs Oyster: Which Global Hiring Platform Is Right for You?
summary: Deel vs Oyster compared by Ontop: fees, features, and which platform actually fits your global hiring needs.
body_text: Managing a global team gets complicated fast. Compliance rules, contractor agreements, and payroll systems vary by country, and picking the wrong platform can cost a company time and money. Two names consistently surface in the conversation around the best international payroll software: Deel and Oyster. Both simplify global hiring and cross-border payments, but they differ in pricing, structure, and the types of teams they serve best. Understanding those differences matters before committing to either platform. Deel leans heavily into employer-of-record services and full-time employee compliance, while Oyster targets companies building distributed teams, with a focus on benefits and local contracts. For businesses that primarily pay international contractors, payroll software from Ontop offers a leaner alternative designed for speed and simplicity. Table of Contents Why Most Companies Compare the Wrong Things What Are Deel and Oyster? Deel vs Oyster: Key Differences That Matter for Growing Companies The Hidden Costs Companies Often Miss When Choosing a Global Hiring Platform How to Choose the Right Platform for Your Global Team How Ontop Helps Companies Simplify Global Hiring and Payroll Book a Demo Today - See why 950+ Companies Trust OnTop to Power their Global Teams Summary Most global hiring comparisons focus on pricing grids and country coverage maps, but those metrics miss the friction points that actually slow teams down. New business applications surged to over 5 million in 2023, up from roughly 3.5 million in 2019 (U.S. Census Bureau Business Formation Statistics), meaning more companies than ever are building distributed teams from the start. For those teams, a mismatched platform choice creates compounding delays across every new hire, every new country, and every missed payroll deadline. Deel and Oyster take meaningfully different approaches to global employment infrastructure. Oyster reports that over 80% of its hires are employed directly by its own entities rather than through third-party partners, thereby tightening local compliance accountability. Deel, founded in 2019 and valued at $12 billion, has expanded aggressively into contractor management, multi-currency payments, and a broader suite of HR tools, making it a denser system with more configuration options but also more complexity for smaller people operations teams to manage. The hidden cost of global hiring rarely appears in a pricing comparison. Employer costs can exceed salary by up to 30% or more depending on the country (Thomson Reuters Tax and Accounting), and when fragmented tooling is layered on top of that baseline, the operational drag multiplies. HR teams chase data instead of managing people, finance teams spend payroll week reconciling disconnected systems, and the true cost of each hire grows well beyond what most finance models account for. Worker experience is a retention variable that most platform evaluations ignore entirely. Research from HireD AI App found that 57% of candidates lose interest in a role if the hiring process takes too long, and that attrition continues into onboarding and the first payroll cycle. A contractor who waits weeks to get set up or receives payment through a slow wire with an opaque exchange rate is already reconsidering their commitment, and that signal rarely shows up until someone has already left. Workforce structure should drive the platform decision, not feature counts or country lists. A company running 40 contractors across Southeast Asia and Latin America needs different infrastructure than one hiring full-time employees through an EOR in Germany. Forcing a contractor-heavy operation through an EOR-first platform means paying for a compliance architecture not designed for that model and absorbing the administrative burden that comes with it. Scalability is not about how many countries a platform lists on its homepage. What matters is how the platform performs when payroll runs across four currencies, three new hires are onboarding in the same week, and every added country introduces new classification rules. Platforms built primarily around EOR infrastructure tend to introduce approval layers and legal review cycles that slow the process, while contractor-first architectures remove steps rather than adding them as headcount grows. Payroll software helps teams address this by consolidating contractor payments, compliance workflows, and worker financial access into a single flow, so the operational cost of adding a new country does not multiply with each hire. Why Most Companies Compare the Wrong Things Pricing grids and country lists dominate most Deel vs Oyster comparisons. Teams line up the numbers and decide based on whichever EOR coverage map looks more complete. That feels like doing your homework. It isn't. "Choosing an EOR based on pricing grids and country coverage alone is like choosing a bank based on the color of its app — you're optimizing for the wrong variable entirely." ⚠️ Warning: Comparing platforms on coverage maps and price points alone means you're missing the factors that actually determine whether your global hiring succeeds or stalls. 🎯 Key Point: The real differentiators between Deel and Oyster lie beneath the surface — in compliance depth , onboarding speed , and support quality — none of which appear on a pricing grid . Pricing grids → Total cost of ownership : Shift focus from initial invoice price to the full lifecycle cost, including hidden FX margins, operational labor, and maintenance. Country coverage maps → Compliance depth per country : Evaluate the provider's ability to navigate local regulations and licensing, rather than just the number of countries on a map. Feature checklists → Onboarding speed & support quality : Prioritize how quickly the team can get up and running and the level of expert guidance provided during issues. Surface-level specs → Real-world reliability : Look beyond theoretical transfer speeds to verified payment success rates, fraud defense, and system resilience. ‍ ‍ Why is global hiring more than a compliance transaction? Global hiring has never been about following rules alone. It's an ongoing system in which problems that slow down teams rarely appear on price lists. According to Fortune, citing U.S. Census Bureau Business Formation Statistics , new business applications jumped to over 5 million in 2023, up from about 3.5 million in 2019, indicating that more companies are building teams across multiple locations from the start. For those companies, the cost of a slow, fragmented payroll process compounds with each new worker and new country. What does a fragmented payroll setup actually cost growing teams? Most teams cobble together solutions: one platform for EOR, another for contractor payments, a spreadsheet for tracking. As the number of workers grows across different locations, this mix of tools creates onboarding delays, payroll errors requiring manual fixes, and HR teams spending hours locating data that should update automatically. Payroll software built around contractor-first infrastructure consolidates payments, compliance, and worker financial tools into a single flow, so the operational cost of adding a new country doesn't multiply with each hire. What the wrong comparison actually costs The hidden cost isn't the monthly fee—it's the administrative drag from a mismatched platform. An EOR arrangement requiring three weeks to activate in a new market becomes a recruiting disadvantage when candidates have competing offers. According to Fortune, citing the U.S. Small Business Administration , small businesses with fewer than 500 employees account for 99.9% of all U.S. businesses, and for those companies, delayed hires or payroll errors hit harder without a large HR team to absorb the impact. Does the comparison assume full-time employment is the default? The deeper issue is that EOR-heavy comparisons assume full-time employment is the default. A growing share of global talent prefers contractor arrangements , and many companies prefer them for flexibility, speed, and cost. When both platforms are optimized for EOR compliance rather than contractor-first speed, the comparison rests on an outdated assumption. What should you actually be evaluating in a payroll platform? What matters is whether the platform helps you move fast, pay reliably , and keep workers engaged. This requires understanding what each platform was built to do. Deel and Oyster are global employment platforms that solve an important problem: hiring talent in countries where you have no legal presence . Both act as the legal employer on your behalf , handling payroll, taxes, benefits, and compliance so you can bring on workers in new markets without setting up a local business entity . "Global employment platforms like Deel and Oyster exist to remove the single biggest barrier to international hiring — the legal requirement to establish a local entity before you can pay anyone." — Core EOR Value Proposition 🎯 Key Point: Both Deel and Oyster operate as Employer of Record (EOR) platforms — meaning they become the official legal employer so your company doesn't have to. 💡 What This Means in Practice: Instead of spending months and thousands of dollars incorporating a foreign entity, you can hire a worker in a new country in a matter of days . Legal Employer Status: The provider acts as the Employer of Record (EOR), absorbing all local employment liability and protecting your company from jurisdictional risks. Payroll Processing: Ensures workers are paid in full compliance with local regulations and in the correct local currency , eliminating manual conversion errors. Tax Compliance: Automates the complex process of calculating, withholding, and remitting local taxes, handling all obligations automatically . Benefits Administration: Manages the entire lifecycle of both statutory and supplemental benefits , ensuring your talent remains compliant and competitive in the local market. No Local Entity Needed: Allows your business to enter new international markets rapidly without the high cost and time investment of establishing a foreign legal entity. ‍ ‍ How do Deel and Oyster actually work? The mechanics are similar: you identify the candidate, the platform employs them through its legal infrastructure, and you manage the work relationship. Deel operates in more than 150 countries, while Oyster operates in more than 180. According to the Oyster HR vs Deel Compare Page , over 80% of hires through Oyster are employed directly through Oyster's own entities, reducing reliance on third-party partners and strengthening compliance accountability at the local level. How each platform got here Deel was founded in 2019 and reached a $12 billion valuation through aggressive expansion across contractor management, global payroll , and HR tools. Oyster positioned itself around distributed-first employment with emphasis on owned entities and structured compliance workflows. Why do most platform comparisons miss the point? Most teams evaluate these platforms against the same checklist: country coverage, EOR pricing, onboarding speed, contractor support, and payroll reliability. This reduces meaningful differences to a spreadsheet comparison rather than a strategic decision. Where does the real friction show up at scale? Companies typically evaluate global hiring tools based on current needs rather than future scalability. A platform that handles five hires smoothly can create problems at fifty, especially when managing multiple currencies, diverse local benefits, and varying contractor classification rules across jurisdictions. Both Deel and Oyster offer contractor management alongside EOR services, but the experience of paying a contractor in Lagos or Bogotá—and providing reliable ways to receive, spend, and move those funds—is where most EOR-first comparisons stop asking important questions. Platforms like Ontop build financial infrastructure around contractor needs rather than layering it onto an EOR model designed primarily for full-time employment. The useful comparison isn't which platform has more features, but which one fits how you hire and how your workers want to get paid. Deel vs Oyster Key Differences That Matter for Growing Companies The sharpest differences between Deel and Oyster show up in critical moments : when your payroll team chases a payment discrepancy at 11pm , or when a new hire in an unfamiliar country waits days for a contract that should take hours . "The real test of any global HR platform isn't what it promises on a sales call — it's how it performs when time-sensitive problems demand immediate answers ." — HR Operations Insight Late-night payroll support: Deel offers 24/7 live assistance , whereas Oyster often relies on limited off-hours access , which can delay urgent issues. Contract turnaround time: Deel typically delivers contracts in hours , while Oyster's process can take days , potentially impacting time-sensitive hiring. Unfamiliar country onboarding: Both platforms excel here, with Deel providing built-in local compliance and Oyster offering strong EOR coverage for complex jurisdictions. Payment discrepancy resolution: Deel provides access to dedicated specialists for immediate fixes, whereas Oyster primarily utilizes a ticket-based system which may extend resolution times. ‍ 🔑 Takeaway: The true differentiator between these platforms isn't their feature lists — it's their response speed and reliability when your team faces high-stakes, time-sensitive situations. 💡 Tip: Before committing to either platform, always test their support responsiveness outside of business hours — this is when critical payroll issues are most likely to surface for globally distributed teams . ‍ Where payroll infrastructure actually diverges Deel has built significant in-house payroll infrastructure across many markets, reducing handoffs to third-party processors and centralizing visibility into payment flows. For companies managing payroll across five or more countries, each additional intermediary introduces delays, failures, and reconciliation risks. According to the Native Teams Blog , Deel EOR pricing starts at $599 per employee per month, reflecting this infrastructure investment. Oyster's model relies on direct entity ownership, with Oyster reporting that over 80% of hires are employed directly through its own entities rather than third-party partners. This distinction shapes how compliance risk is managed and how quickly issues are resolved in specific countries. How does compliance support actually work when it matters most? The failure point is not whether a platform offers compliance support, but whether that support is fast and specific enough when hiring in countries with unusual termination rules, mandatory benefit structures, or worker classification gray zones. Deel's contractor management tools cover misclassification risk, localized contract generation, and multi-currency payment flexibility across contractor and employee relationships. Oyster leverages its entity-ownership model as a compliance advantage, arguing that direct employment through owned entities reduces reliance on local partners with inconsistent standards. Both reduce legal exposure through different mechanisms: the right choice depends on whether your workforce skews toward full-time employment or contractor-heavy structures. When does EOR no longer make sense for your team? Most growing companies choose EOR because it feels like the safest option. But EOR was built for a workforce that doesn't align with how global talent operates today. When most of your international hires are contractors, paying $599+ per person per month for full employment infrastructure adds cost without matching benefits. Our payroll software , built for contractor-first teams, handles compliance, payments, and onboarding without treating every engagement as an employment situation, enabling faster activation and lower cost per hire. It shows up as hours your HR team spends finding workarounds, delayed onboarding that frustrates new hires, and reporting gaps that force finance teams to build their own spreadsheets. Deel's broader, feature-rich platform delivers genuine power for teams that need it, but creates complexity that smaller people operations teams may struggle to manage. Oyster's design philosophy favors a cleaner, more guided experience suited for companies that want global hiring to feel straightforward rather than configurable. Scalability is a question about where you're going, not where you are The right platform for 20 international employees may not be the right platform for 200. Deel's investment in workforce management tooling —across HR functions, equity management, and device management—positions it as a system that scales with operational complexity. Oyster's strength lies in the quality and directness of its employment relationships, a meaningful advantage for companies prioritizing depth of compliance over breadth of features. Scalability extends beyond country coverage or headcount capacity to whether the platform's architecture matches your workforce's shape as it grows and whether the cost structure remains viable when running payroll across a dozen time zones. Yet even after mapping every feature and weighing every pricing tier, a cost category remains uncalculated before signing a contract . When onboarding, payroll, compliance, and document management are handled in separate systems, the administrative burden multiplies rather than adds value. Managers coordinate across platforms rather than manage people. Finance teams spend payroll week chasing data instead of validating it. These slow, invisible drains never appear on a pricing comparison spreadsheet. What happens when workarounds stop being enough? Most teams handle this by adding more people or workarounds: another coordinator, another spreadsheet, another manual check before payroll closes. This feels manageable until the team grows from 15 international contractors to 60. That's when the platform architecture either holds or it doesn't. Payroll software built around a contractor-first model sidesteps much of this by removing the EOR layer entirely where it isn't legally required, meaning fewer handoffs, faster payments, and a cleaner experience for workers. Yet the worker's experience of getting paid, accessing funds, and managing finances across borders is a retention variable hiding in plain sight. For the contractor, payment is where the relationship either strengthens or quietly breaks down. What does a frictionless global payroll experience actually look like? title: Carrier Abound Wins a 2025 Sustainability Leadership Award for Digitally Transforming Building Operations
summary: Discover how Carrier Abound’s AI-powered platform helped retailers save over 667 million kWh of energy, prevent 161,300 lbs of refrigerant leakage, and enhance operations across 33,000+ stores, earning the 2025 Sustainability Leadership Award.
body_text: KENNESAW, Ga., August 21, 2025 — Carrier Abound, part of Carrier Global Corporation (NYSE: CARR), global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, has been awarded a 2025 Sustainability Leadership Award by the Business Intelligence Group. The recognition is for its forward-thinking approach and measurable impact in driving sustainable building operations through Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) solutions. Now in its 10th year, the Sustainability Awards celebrate companies that are making a measurable difference in building a more sustainable future. This year’s edition honored organizations leading the way in net-zero strategies, climate equity, and AI-powered transformation. The award underscores Carrier's commitment to helping retailers minimize the carbon footprint of their store operations through the renowned AI-powered Abound Insights platform, backed by global command centers. This comprehensive solution tackles issues like fragmented data, manual operations, and ineffective maintenance practices by creating smart ecosystems that can analyze information, make informed decisions, and automate routine tasks. Presently, Carrier Abound supports multi-site clients in enhancing operations across more than 33,000 stores globally. “We are honored and proud to receive the 2025 Sustainability Leadership Award,” said Yasir Qureshi, General Manager, Carrier Abound. “This recognition further strengthens our purpose and reflects our deep commitment to creating a lasting impact – for our customers, for the future generations to come, and for the world we share.” In the past 12 months, Carrier Abound enabled retailers to save over 667 million kWh of energy globally, reduce emissions from truck rolls and HVAC refrigerant leakage, and build more efficient and future-ready operations. For a leading retailer with over 2,100 stores in North America, refrigerant leaks were identified across approximately 5,300 rooftop units (RTUs) from May 2024 to September 2024. Timely intervention helped save over 161,300 pounds of refrigerant1 from further leakage, reducing emissions while preserving equipment health and ensuring operational continuity. For more information on Abound solutions, please visit www.abound.carrier.com . 1Estimated 89.6% of total RTU capacity across all the 5,300 RTUs. About Carrier Abound Carrier Abound provides digitally connected lifecycle solutions and services for diverse building portfolios. The solutions and services enable building management to see deeply and broadly across their assets, prioritize and act on real-time insights, and refine, adapt, and scale on a continual basis to improve energy efficiency and asset performance, enhance occupant comfort and productivity, and streamline compliance reporting. Carrier Abound is part of Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions. For more information, please visit abound.carrier.com or follow on social media at @CarrierAbound .

title: Engineered Building Solutions Powering the New Era of Critical Infrastructure
body_text: NEWS ARTICLE Engineered Building Solutions Powering the New Era of Critical Infrastructure Learn More Across industries, demands on critical electrical infrastructure are intensifying. What was once a network of wires and equipment has evolved into the backbone of modern life—powering hospitals, manufacturing, utilities, and the rapidly expanding digital economy. Today, organizations are struggling to navigate rising electricity loads, accelerating data center growth, aging infrastructure, and increasing expectations for resilience, safety, and speed. The scale and complexity of today’s challenges require a more integrated, forward-looking approach to electrification. That’s where nVent is delivering value through engineered buildings, switchgear systems, and bus systems—three core solution areas that work together to create safer, smarter, and more resilient infrastructure environments. Engineered Buildings: Enabling Faster Electrification at Scale One of the biggest challenges in electrification is deploying new infrastructure quickly enough to meet rising demand. Traditional construction methods often create delays, labor constraints, and inconsistent quality. nVent’s engineered building solutions help overcome these barriers through modular, prefabricated designs that accelerate deployment timelines and simplify infrastructure expansion. Solutions such as e-houses, modular substations, BESS enclosures, and power distribution centers provide fully integrated environments for electrical systems, controls, and energy management technologies. Because these systems are engineered and assembled off-site, customers can simplify construction while improving standardization and quality control. The technology behind these modular systems allows customers to standardize infrastructure while still tailoring solutions to specific operational requirements. Each building is custom engineered to optimize power distribution, environmental performance, physical security, and operational efficiency. This approach helps organizations scale infrastructure more predictably while supporting sustainability goals through reduced waste, improved energy efficiency, and streamlined construction processes. For customers, the benefits are significant: faster time to operation, lower project risk, enhanced reliability, and the flexibility to adapt infrastructure as business needs evolve. Switchgear Systems: Delivering Safe and Reliable Power Distribution Reliable power distribution is increasingly critical to operational continuity. nVent’s switchgear systems are designed to help power be managed safely, efficiently, and consistently across demanding environments. nVent offers a comprehensive range of medium-voltage and low-voltage switchgear solutions engineered to meet application-specific requirements and industry standards, including UL and IEEE compliance. These systems can be customized for diverse operational environments, helping customers address unique performance, capacity, and safety requirements. A key differentiator is nVent’s focus on protection and resilience. Arc-resistant switchgear designs aligned with ANSI and NEMA requirements help minimize risk to personnel and equipment by containing and redirecting hazardous energy during electrical faults. This added layer of safety is especially important in industries where uninterrupted operations and worker protection are non-negotiable. Beyond performance, these technologies help organizations improve operational reliability, reduce downtime, and strengthen overall infrastructure resilience. By integrating advanced engineering with rigorous safety standards, nVent enables customers to operate with greater confidence in increasingly complex power environments. Bus Systems: Supporting Continuous and Efficient Power Flow Reliable power transmission is foundational to modern infrastructure, particularly in industries where even brief interruptions can have significant operational and financial consequences. nVent’s bus system solutions are designed to support uninterrupted, high-efficiency power distribution across a broad range of applications. Medium-voltage and high-voltage bus systems are engineered to meet stringent reliability standards while supporting the growing demands of electrified infrastructure, industrial modernization, and digital operations. These systems provide a flexible and efficient method for distributing large amounts of electrical power while helping optimize system performance and space utilization. What distinguishes nVent’s approach is its full lifecycle support model. Customers receive support from initial engineering and system design through manufacturing, installation, upgrades, replacement parts, and emergency services. This end-to-end partnership ensures infrastructure remains reliable, maintainable, and adaptable over time. The result is a power distribution ecosystem built not only for today’s operational demands, but for long-term resilience and future growth. Expanding Capabilities Through Strategic Growth Through two large-scale acquisitions, nVent expanded its capabilities and strengthened its position as a leader in engineered building, switchgear, and bus solutions as a trusted partner to customers worldwide. The nVent TRACHTE brand provides a strong foundation in engineered buildings and system protection. Known for custom-engineered control building solutions, it strengthens nVent’s enclosures portfolio and expands its ability to serve key industries, including power utilities, data centers, and renewable energy. Building on this, a 2025 acquisition of an electrical products group—including enclosure systems, switchgear systems, and bus systems—enhanced the portfolio adding approximately 1,100 employees, nine U.S. manufacturing facilities, and a large installed base across utilities, OEMs, data centers, and EPCs. These strategic additions build on more than 125 years of combined industry experience and bring together respected legacy brands, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and specialized expertise. The result is a more connected and comprehensive offering designed to meet the realities of modern infrastructure projects. From early discovery through delivery and lifecycle support, nVent provides an even more unified partnership model, helping customers design, build, and scale with confidence. A More Connected Portfolio, Built Around Customers Through its connected portfolio, nVent brings together engineered buildings, switchgear, and bus solutions in a more integrated approach designed to streamline, improve coordination, and support faster project delivery. What differentiates nVent is not only the breadth of its portfolio, but the depth of support behind it. Customers work with dedicated technical specialists and experienced project teams from early planning through post-installation support, helping ensure alignment throughout the project lifecycle. Combined with flexible, engineering-led customization and strategically located manufacturing operations, nVent is positioned to deliver reliable, application-specific solutions that help customers navigate evolving infrastructure challenges with greater confidence. Beyond these core areas, customers gain access to the full nVent portfolio—solutions that connect and protect critical infrastructure globally. The result is a more seamless, integrated approach that reduces complexity and accelerates project delivery. Leading the Future of Engineered Infrastructure The challenges facing critical electrical infrastructure markets are only growing in scale and urgency. Meeting them requires more than products—it requires integrated solutions, deep expertise, and a partner committed to long-term success. Through strategic acquisitions and continued investment in innovation and manufacturing, nVent has strengthened its ability to meet this moment. By bringing together expanded capabilities across engineered buildings, switchgear, and bus systems, nVent is helping customers keep pace with change and lead through it. Engineered buildings accelerate infrastructure deployment by using modular, prefabricated designs assembled off-site. This approach reduces construction time, improves quality control, and simplifies expansion. As a result, organizations can bring electrical systems online faster, lower project risk, and scale electrification more efficiently to meet growing demand. Why are switchgear systems critical for power reliability and safety? Switchgear systems are critical because they manage and protect electrical power distribution. Advanced designs, including arc-resistant technology, help prevent equipment damage and reduce risks to personnel during faults. This ensures consistent power delivery, minimizes downtime, and supports safe operations in environments where reliability is essential. What role do bus systems play in modern electrical infrastructure? Bus systems enable efficient, high-capacity power distribution across facilities. title: Find Your Summer Signature Scent with this Fragrance Quiz
summary: Not sure what to wear in the heat? Take the Scentbird fragrance quiz to find your summer signature scent, matched to your fragrance family and mood.
body_text: Perfume isn’t one-and-done. It’s an ever-evolving situationship, and nothing stirs the pot like a change in weather. All those fragrances you were happy to go steady with for autumn, through the winter holidays, and into spring… come July, they don’t stand a chance at being your summer signature scent. Part of it is, when the temperature rises and the sun comes out, so does the summer version of us. (We like to think of her as more fun than our winter self). We want to wear the clothes we only get to wear in the heat, spend more time outside, and feel all… summery. But the hot weather doesn’t just change how we feel and act. It also changes how your perfume behaves—it pushes scent louder, turns sweet notes syrupy, and burns the light stuff off by noon. We need scents that are built for the heat. So you’re thinking, okay, I need to find my signature scent for summer, sure. But where to start? What perfume should I wear when it’s 90 degrees out? Well, surprise, we’ve got the answer. And it’s easy: take the Scentbird perfume quiz . Meet the Fragrance Families The first thing you’ll learn from the quiz is what kind of fragrance family you’re best suited to. Let’s do a quick recap: Fresh Clean, airy scents built on notes like cotton , mint , and green leaves; crisp and weightless, which is why they work best in heat. Picture the feeling of a cool summer shower you didn’t want to step out of—the kind of scent that feels refreshing on a blazing-hot day, when anything heavier would just be too much. Citrus Bright, zesty scents led by lemon , bergamot , grapefruit , and orange; sharp and energizing, but they fade fast, so reapplication is part of the deal. These scents feel like cracking open something cold and fizzy on a hot day. This is the instantly wide-awake option—the one to reach for on a sluggish, sticky morning when you need a rejuvenating citrusy reset. Aquatic Cool, clean scents that recreate water , sea air , and rain through marine notes like calone, for a blue, just-out-of-the-ocean feel. All the cool freshness of a summer swim (with none of the sand or salty hair). When the heat feels inescapable, this is the fragrance family that feels like a long drink of water. Solar-gourmand Sweet, edible notes like vanilla , coconut , and caramel met with warm solar accords that mimic sunshine on skin; smells like sunscreen, sand, and a tropical vacation. This is summer’s sweet tooth—golden, a little hedonistic, like a coconut dessert at a beach bar. Best after dark, when you want warmth without weight. Light floral Soft, fresh flowers like neroli, freesia , peony , and orange blossom ; the airier, less heady side of florals—perfect for warm weather. Florals, but make it summer. This is the easy-wearing, hard-to-get-wrong family—pretty without being precious, and just as nice on a Tuesday as for a special occasion. Just a Few Easy Questions The quiz starts with a few easy questions, like the ones below. No overthinking required here, because there are no wrong answers—just give your instinctive response and notice which way you lean. Day or night? A sparkling-bright citrus or fresh scent for daylight; or something warmer and deliciously skin-close for once the sun goes down. (We can’t lie, it’s pretty great having one of each). Fresh or sweet? Cool and clean (aquatic, green, citrus), or warm as summer sunshine and a little edible (solar-gourmand)? This is one of the big either-ors—this question splits your whole summer wardrobe in two. Subtle or statement? A quiet scent that stays close, or one that announces you from across the rooftop bar? Heat amplifies everything, so a “statement” in July hits louder than it would in December. Signature or rotation? One summer scent you wear on repeat, or a little lineup you switch between by mood and plan? Familiar or adventurous? There’s a lot to be said for a safe bet you already know you love—but then again, something nobody else at the party is wearing is kind of exciting too (summer’s a good time to try the second one). Answer those and just like that, you’ve sketched the shape of your ideal summer fragrance. Once you’ve completed the Scentbird fragrance quiz, not only will you know what kind of fragrance family suits you best but you’ll be given a list of specific scent recommendations for your new summer signature scent. The Quiz’s Best Friend: Your Scentbird Fragrance Subscription And once the fragrance quiz has given you a list of scents that are a great fit for your taste, the best way to try them is with your Scentbird perfume subscription . With over 1000 authentic scents right at your fingertips, a Scentbird subscription is an easy and cost-effective way to try a huge variety of fragrances. Here’s why that beats buying blind. A full bottle is a commitment you make before you’ve worn the thing past the first spray—and fragrance doesn’t sit still. Notes shift over a few hours, then shift again in the heat, so the scent that won you over on a paper strip can turn into someone else’s by lunch. A vial gives you a month of real wear—through commutes, heat, and actual summer days—to find out if it’s love before you spend on a full bottle. Date it before you marry it. With this fragrance quiz and a Scentbird subscription , your new summer signature scent is just a few clicks away. Frequently asked questions How do I find my summer signature scent? Start by identifying the fragrance family that suits you, then test a few scents on skin in real summer conditions. The Scentbird quiz does the first step for you, matching your preferences to a family and giving specific recommendations you can try before committing to a bottle. What fragrance families work best in hot weather? Fresh, citrus, aquatic, and light floral scents work best in heat because they are lighter and more refreshing. Solar-gourmand scents also suit summer, especially after dark, when you want warmth without heaviness. Why does my perfume smell different in summer? Heat pushes fragrance to project louder, turns sweet notes syrupy, and burns off lighter top notes faster. That is why scents you loved in winter can feel like too much in July, and why lighter, heat-friendly families tend to wear better in summer. How does the Scentbird fragrance quiz work? The quiz asks a few quick preference questions, such as day or night and fresh or sweet, then matches you to a fragrance family and a list of specific scent recommendations. You can try those scents through a Scentbird subscription before buying a full bottle. Featured Image: Maison d’Etto .

body_text: Key Takeaways The comprehensive Standard® Gas Fuel Injection program includes over 1,100 all-new, not remanufactured, Gasoline Direct Injectors, as well as related components All Standard® Fuel Injectors undergo extensive testing including initial life-cycle validation and 100% end-of-line testing Standard® GDI High-Pressure Fuel Pumps are expertly manufactured and tested to help optimize performance, even in high-heat environments NEW YORK, N.Y., May 8, 2026 - Standard Motor Products, Inc. All Standard® Fuel Injectors undergo extensive testing including initial life-cycle validation and 100% end-of-line testing. This comprehensive testing regimen involves more than 35 different tests and inspections including endurance, spray pattern, thermal cycles, vibration, shock load, dynamic and static flow, and more. Popular applications include the 2025-20 Nissan Frontier, and 2025-21 Subaru Crosstrek. Additionally, MFI Fuel Injector Multi-Packs are available, covering over 31 million vehicles, for a complete repair solution. GDI systems rely on a constant supply of fuel at high pressure. Standard® GDI High-Pressure Fuel Pumps are expertly manufactured and tested to help optimize performance, even in high-heat environments. For long-term durability, Standard® High-Pressure Fuel Pumps feature precision-manufactured stainless steel internal components and high-temperature seals. Each pump is precision-engineered to optimize GDI performance, and lab tested and validated on actual vehicles to ensure performance and longevity. Over 115 SKUs are currently available for import and domestic vehicles. Additionally, Blue Streak® GDI High-Pressure Fuel Pump Kits include everything needed for a high-pressure fuel pump service in one box and are available for popular import and domestic applications. GDI High-Pressure Fuel Pumps have recently been released for popular Audi and Volkswagen vehicles like the 2025-20 Audi Q3 and the 2024-19 Volkswagen Jetta, as well as 1.2 million BMW vehicles through the 2025 model-year. John Herc, Vice President of Vehicle Control Marketing at SMP, stated, “The Standard® Fuel Injection Program is constantly expanding as we are regularly adding new Fuel Injectors, GDI High-Pressure Fuel Pumps and other related components. Our program is the most comprehensive in the industry, and we are working hard to keep it that way for our distribution partners and for the technicians who depend on Standard®.” All Standard® Gas Fuel Injectors and fuel injection components are listed in the catalog found at StandardBrand.com and in electronic catalog providers.
